questions.stem: A point $P(3, 2)$ is reflected in the $y$-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
questions.explanation: Reflecting in the $y$-axis changes the sign of the $x$-coordinate while the $y$-coordinate stays the same. So $(3, 2) \to (-3, 2)$.

questions.stem: A point $Q(4, 1)$ is reflected in the line $y = x$. What are the coordinates of the image?
questions.explanation: Reflecting in the line $y = x$ swaps the $x$ and $y$ coordinates. So $(4, 1) \to (1, 4)$.

questions.stem: Under a reflection, which of the following changes?
questions.explanation: A reflection is an isometry, so lengths, angles, and area are all preserved. However, the orientation (sense) is reversed — a clockwise labelling becomes anticlockwise.
